ia_wild_iowa_wall.blurb: Wild Iowa Wall is a limestone cliff in the Pictured Rocks county park, a minute or two along the main trail from the car park. It is a short, steep face with a vertical crack splitting an overhang, so the climbing is powerful rather than long. Most of the 18 lines are bolted sport climbs, with a few trad lines, one top-rope and a handful of boulder problems from about V2 to V5. The roped climbs cluster in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with only a couple of easier ones. Tree cover keeps it shady, and it draws a crowd on good weekends. Fall and spring are the comfortable seasons.
